items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: if you accompany somewhat differently playing behind an instrumentalist, Dizzy Gillespie or Sonny Stitt, as you do a vocalist?

ctx.x: And let me tell you, one day I came home and, you know, they’re not always great days, and something must have happened at school because I came home and complained. And my wife says, “What do you expect to have fun every day?” I said, “Yeah, okay, this is what I do.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

I was fascinated by, you’re talking about accompaniment, because one of my questions I had here was if you accompany somewhat differently playing behind an instrumentalist, Dizzy Gillespie or Sonny Stitt, as you do a vocalist? You started, I think you may have answered it but what would be the difference?

Well when you’re playing with guys like Dizzy they’re constantly changing directions. It’s just — when you’re working with singers you know they don’t change directions too much. They’re pretty much melody singers or they’ll scat a chorus or something like that but they don’t really divert from, they don’t divert from the tune too much. But guys like Dizzy, you know, every note has got the possibility of going somewhere else so it’s — what happens when you play with guys like that you have to play less and less…
